text:
sre-bot: [ALERT] p99 streaming stalls detected for /v1/chat/stream across prod-us-east-1 clusters (>= 10% of requests). Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

olivia: seeing a bunch of SSE clients stuck in HEADERS_RECEIVED -> no chunks. p95 up ~800ms, p99 > 12s.

oncall-jane: on it. I’m pulling logs + checking proxies and LB health. @mike can you watch the runtime side?

mike: yep. starting tail on model-workers and proxy-logs. running `kubectl logs -l app=stream-proxy -n prod --since=15m` to confirm.

rafael: checking envoy metrics now. early guess: TLS sessions not being drained properly, or upstream backpressure. seeing increased `upstream_cx_idle_timeout` in envoy.

lydia: flagged top 3 customers on pager duty. one SME reporting UI timeouts in support. looks like chat sessions show "waiting for response" spinner stuck.

olivia: good call. are we seeing any burst of 429s or connection resets from clients? metrics show 2xx count steady but chunk events low.

mike: observed high queue depth in the serving runtime for chunking stage. logs show repeated `KVCache` contention errors around the same time. snippet:

```
ERROR runtime/chunker.go:219 handleChunk: failed to flush chunk: context deadline exceeded
WARN runtime/kvcache.go:87 getOrCreate: lock contention, wait=6.1s
```

olivia: that fits intake->chunker queuing. could be client backpressure (slow reads) causing runtime to hold chunks. any proxy timeouts?

rafael: proxy timeouts configured to 30s keepalive -> envoy has `stream_idle_timeout` 60s. however I see spikes of `downstream_cx_overflow` and `http_connection_manager.downstream_rq_idle_timeout`.

oncall-jane: mitigation plan: 1) enable aggressive chunk flush (force chunking every 200ms) on a small subset of proxies; 2) route traffic for canary customers to fallback variant with shorter max sequence to reduce KV pressure; 3) increase proxy upstream timeout to 90s as temporary. any objections?

mike: +1 for forced flush on a 5% sample. how do we toggle?

olivia: toggle is feature-flag `stream.force_flush_ms`. I'll add patch and do canary rollout via console.

deploy-bot: Deployment started by olivia: patch/stream-force-flush -> prod-us-east-1 (canary 5%). ID: deploy-9876.

rafael: I'm bumping envoy idle timeout to 90s on the affected node pool now. doing node-pool: streaming-proxies-east-1a.

lydia: telling affected customers we have an ongoing mitigation and will update in 30m.

mike: rolled a runtime patch to log slow client read durations. quick code: `metrics.Observe("client_read_ms", readDuration)` in chunker.

olivia: canary shows initial improvement: chunk event rate up ~18% for canary traffic, p99 dropped from 12.3s -> 6.5s. still higher than baseline.

rafael: envoy metrics for canary show downstream timeouts reduced, but upstream queue depth still elevated. KV lock contention persisted in runtime traces, looks like a hot-key pattern for certain prompt prefixes.

mike: hot-key? maybe some clients sending very long repeating prefixes or identical conversation ids causing KV thrash. pulling sample keys.

olivia: got top offending conversation id list and sample payloads. many are retry storms from mobile SDK v1.2.3 where reconnect logic resends open requests.

lydia: opened ticket with SME to ask for SDK update; short-term suggestion: client should back off on reconnect < 3s.

oncall-jane: operational mitigation: 1) apply short lived rate limit per-conversation id on ingress (token bucket 10r/s) 2) extend canary to 25% if numbers hold -> aim to reduce hot-key queueing.

rafael: applying ingress filter now with `lua` filter to enforce per-convo token bucket. rolling to 25% of proxies.

deploy-bot: Rollout success: proxy-filter-ingress -> canary 25%. ID: deploy-9880.

olivia: after ingress throttling, p99 dropped further to ~2.1s for canary cluster. production aggregate still at ~3.8s but improving.

mike: backlog drain observed on runtime workers across canary nodes. KV contention gone for the top keys. good signal.

lydia: support update sent to customers. some clients report immediate improvements. one customer still sees intermittent stalls — collecting logs.

oncall-jane: next steps: 1) keep canary config and ingress filter; 2) schedule a controlled SDK update campaign; 3) add longer-term fix in runtime to shard KV caches by convo hash to avoid single-key hotspots. assigning to @mike and @rafael.

olivia: creating follow-up issues: #INC-4587 (runtime KV sharding), #INC-4588 (client SDK reconnect guidance), #INC-4589 (proxy default timeouts review). adding timeline and owners.

mike: noted. will start design doc for KV sharding.

rafael: documenting mitigation runbook so oncall can toggle ingress throttling and force flush flags. adding a rollout knob in console.

deploy-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> partial_recovery.

oncall-jane: handing off to next on-call (olivia) — I'm stepping out in 45m. details: mitigations in place, canary expanded to 25%, p99 trending down but continue monitoring 2h for regression. please update incident board and postmortem if needed. :white_check_mark:

olivia: thanks @oncall-jane. I'll take over monitoring and coordinate the PM/CS comms. further notes: customer impact window ~ 2026-08-21T14:00:00Z -> ongoing, most customers back to normal.

mike: added `trace_id=chunk-starvation-2489012345` to traces for follow-up.

sre-bot: [LOG] incident acknowledged by oncall-jane at 2489012351. severity: P2, impacted_apis: [/v1/chat/stream], current_state: partial_recovery.

lydia: final note — CS will reach out to top-5 customers with a short RCA once postmortem is ready.

olivia: I'll open the postmortem draft and start capturing timelines. good job team. :clap:
